This app: the HUD, the voice announcer, the rules and the settings.
Reads the radio's channels and telemetry. Its libraries are included in the app, as RadioMaster's manual describes for app developers. Its repository states no license, and RadioMaster has not answered my questions about redistribution (see the notice in the README). Thank you, RadioMaster, for publishing it.
The Qt libraries that come with the RadioMaster SDK, as delivered with it. Source code: download.qt.io.
The C++ runtime of the Android NDK, needed by the SDK.
The standard library of the Kotlin language, which the app is written in.
The typeface of the menus, settings and all running text, in four weights (trimmed to the letters the app needs).
The narrow typeface of the titles and the big numbers, in two weights (trimmed to the letters the app needs).
The font of the Chinese texts, cut down to the characters the app's Chinese texts use. It is used only when the language is Chinese, so that Chinese shows on radios that have no Chinese font.

Welcome to AX-HUD
AX-HUD shows the video from the HDMI input of your AX12 full screen, with a HUD on top, and speaks announcements and warnings. It only reads from the radio and never writes to it. This guide takes about a minute.
Allow the camera
The HDMI input reaches Android as a camera, so AX-HUD needs the camera permission. If you said no by mistake, allow it in the Android settings, under Apps, AX-HUD, Permissions. Without it you see the gray No video screen.
The first data takes about 12 seconds
After you open the app, the radio data (sticks, link quality, telemetry) appears after about 12 seconds. That wait is inside the RadioMaster SDK and is not an error. A banner counts the seconds. The video starts at once.
Where everything is
Tap MENU at the top right for nine tiles: Sound rules, Speech, Battery, Aircraft, Sunlight, Dashboard, Flight logs, Settings and Exit. Choose your aircraft and battery pack first, because their limits drive the warnings. Sunlight: dark text on light, for direct sun. Settings holds the overlays, the layout, the checks, the flight logs, the languages and the updates.
An aid, not a safety system
AX-HUD helps you see and hear what your aircraft is doing. Do not rely on it as your only warning. Always fly within your local rules.
No position in this log, so there is no 3D view.

Describe the problem (optional)
OK
Whole minutes from 1 to 240, at most 8, for example 30,15,10,5,2,1. Empty means no warnings; the end of the window is always spoken.
Warn at (minutes left)
Use whole minutes from 1 to 240, at most 8, for example 30,15,10,5,2,1.
Arm switch channel (1 to 16, AUX1 is channel 5)
Counts as armed at or above (microseconds)
Counts as disarmed below (microseconds)
The gap between the two thresholds stops a bump of the switch from arming or disarming the statistics. The switch must stay put for 0.3 seconds.
Arm detection
The channel is 1 to 16
Use microseconds, with the disarmed value not above the armed one

Current limit line (amps)
Height comes from the GPS altitude relative to where you armed, so expect a few meters of error. The bar turns red when the current is above the limit line.
Flight statistics rows
The current limit is 5 to 300 amps
Left of the sticks
Right of the sticks
On      Channel      Name on the overlay                 Reverse
A bar fills with the channel value. Gray-blue = low, amber = middle, green = high. Names are written along the bar; a short name reads best.\n\nReverse: tick it for a switch that is reversed in the radio, so the bar shows the switch the way you flip it (up = full and green). Only the picture changes: sound and warning rules still use the real channel values.
Channel bars
Defaults
Bar {0}: the channel must be 1 to 16
Mode 1: left = pitch + yaw, right = throttle + roll
Mode 2: left = throttle + yaw, right = pitch + roll
Mode 3: left = throttle + roll, right = pitch + yaw
Mode 4: left = pitch + roll, right = throttle + yaw

Left stick left/right drawn reversed
Right stick up/down drawn reversed
Right stick left/right drawn reversed
The sticks show the channel values the radio sends. Common order: roll 1, pitch 2, throttle 3, yaw 4. Turn a direction round if the dot moves the wrong way.
Channels are numbers from 1 to 16

Text editor
Each check shows a tick when its condition is true and a cross when not, before you arm. The switch on the left turns a check off without deleting it.
A warning shows in the status bar while its condition is true. Critical = red and blinking, warning = amber, info = blue. The switch on the left turns a rule off without deleting it.
A rule speaks when its condition becomes true. The switch on the left turns a rule off without deleting it.
Speech is muted (MENU, Speech)
$low  - warning limit of the active battery profile
$crit  - critical limit
$full  - limit for a full pack

About
Nothing found.
Language
Speech language
The screen and the voice can use different languages. Your rules keep their own words: "Reset the rules to the defaults" loads the starting rules in the voice's language.
Display
Sunlight theme
Shape
The shape of cards, tiles and rows: two cut corners (the default), four cut corners, corner brackets, soft corners or plain rectangles. Warnings keep a solid fill.
Dark text on light backgrounds for the menu, the settings, the other screens and the dashboard, and stronger warnings. In direct sun this reads better than light on dark. The MENU has a Sunlight tile as a quick switch.
Always show the MENU button
Off: the button hides and appears when you touch the screen.
Start-up splash screen (animated, about 3 seconds)
Tap the top edge three times, away from MENU, to save a screenshot to Pictures/AX-HUD.
Active aircraft
Manage the aircraft (add, rename, delete)...
Each aircraft keeps its own rules, warning rules, checks, battery profiles and packs, channel bars, stick mapping and arm switch. Overlay looks, language and updates are shared.
Active battery profile
Edit the packs of this aircraft...
Edit the battery profiles (cells and voltage limits)...
Rules and checks can use the value cell (volts per cell) and the limits $low, $crit and $full of the active profile, for example: cell < $low -> battery low. Switching the profile changes the numbers, not the rules.
The time you are approved to fly, for example the two hours the authority gave you. The radio shows the time left, speaks warnings while the aircraft is armed, and warns when you arm outside the window. It repeats every day and uses the clock of this radio, which says {0} now.
Use an approval window
Two hours from now
Speak the warnings
The value win_left (minutes left, negative after the window has ended) can be used in value cards, charts, rules and logs.
Speak a debrief after landing
After a flight of 20 seconds or more: flight time, distance, capacity used, efficiency, lowest cell and the voltage the pack rests at.
Speak the last position when the link is lost
When the link is lost in flight, a card shows the last position with its distance and bearing from home, and the position is saved on this radio.

Layout of the cards
Move and resize the cards with your finger...
Put every card back in its corner at normal size
Put every card back in its corner at normal size? The places and sizes you chose will be forgotten.
Drag a card to move it and drag its square handle to resize it. Cards that are switched off are not shown. The Size setting of a card is its starting size; resizing multiplies it.
A second page with cards only and no video, for goggles or for a second pair of eyes. Switch pages with the Dashboard tile in the MENU.
Edit the dashboard layout...
Choose a dashboard preset...
Reset the dashboard layout
Replace the dashboard layout with the first one?
Horizon: invert pitch
Horizon: invert roll
Tilt the aircraft nose down: the horizon should show more ground. If it shows the opposite, switch the pitch inversion; the same for roll.
An antenna tracker points your antennas at the aircraft: an ESP32 with two servos, a GPS and a compass. The radio sends the aircraft's position over Bluetooth; the tracker does the pointing. Build instructions: the tracker folder of the project.
Use an antenna tracker
Tracker
Android asks for the location permission to search for Bluetooth devices. AX-HUD does not read your location.
Follow the aircraft
Hold the antennas where they are
Center the antennas (straight ahead)
Test sweep (30 seconds)
Compass calibration: start (turn the tracker through a full circle)
Compass calibration: save
Set the magnetic declination...
Set the antenna height above the launch point...
Writes a log of every flight, from arming to disarming: the values you choose, several rows per second. The files are plain CSV that a spreadsheet opens, and the log viewer can replay them on the radio.
Log every flight
Rows per second
Rows are written up to 20 times a second. The sticks change that often; the values from the aircraft (battery, GPS, attitude) change only as often as your link sends them, about once a second at a slow ELRS telemetry ratio (1:32 at 150 Hz). A faster ratio, such as 1:16 or 1:8, gives a sharper log.
Flights to keep
Flight logs: list, replay and delete...

Swap back to the settings from before the last import? The current settings are kept, so you can swap again.
One file with everything: sound rules, warning rules, checks, overlays, channel bars, battery profiles and language. The sound rules also have their own export above.
If something goes wrong, this page collects what a bug report needs: versions, the device, the state of the radio link and its start-up timing, a digest of the settings and the last events. It holds no GPS positions, no aircraft or pack names and nothing personal. Read it before you send it.
Diagnostics and bug report...
Show the variables panel (every value the radio sends)
Test channels: sliders instead of the radio
Show the start-up timings of the last launches...
The radio link starts on a background thread and keeps running while the app's own screens, file pickers and rebuilds come and go; it stops when you leave the app. The SDK itself needs about 12 seconds to open the radio's serial port; the timings show where the time goes.
Close Settings to see the panels over the video.

Android asks you to confirm every update. The first time it also asks you to allow installs from AX-HUD. Never update during a flight.
